correctness.rationale: PASS: For H without isolated vertices, all faces of the ordinary Lovász open-neighborhood complex of K1∨H have common neighbor either the new universal vertex c (giving Δ(V(H))) or one vertex v∈H (giving c*N(H)). These two subcomplexes have intersection N(H) precisely, where the no-isolates condition ensures the intended vertex ground set. Each part is contractible, inclusions are simplicial cofibrations, and their union is the homotopy pushout of N(H) mapped to two contractible spaces, homotopy equivalent to its unreduced suspension. Repeating addition of universal vertices gives N(K_r∨H)≈Σ^r N(H). For n disjoint cliques Km, N(nKm) is the disjoint union of n boundaries of (m−1)-simplices, each S^{m−2}; suspending n components produces n spheres of dimension m+r−2 and n−1 spheres of dimension r. The friendship-graph case r=1,m=2 thus has 2n−1 circles. Independent small-case graph-common-neighbor homology over GF2 confirmed six representative ranks; these computations are not the all-r proof.
residual_risks: Short cone/suspension identity may be standard folklore or stated in unindexed box-complex/topological graph coloring literature; strong but bounded priority risk.

value.rationale: PASS with moderate value: It is a uniform structural operation rule for arbitrary non-isolated finite H, not an isolated small computation. It supplies immediate homotopy groups and an exact family of graph-join examples including all generalized friendship/windmill graphs, and the suspension recurrence can be reused in topological graph theory. The proof is concise and elementary, so the contribution is an explicit useful lemma, not a major new homotopy technology; no paper-sized theorem or stronger equivariant claim is required.
